newsitem.title: USA: Zomax acquires Trotter, to build CD plant.
newsitem.headline: Zomax acquires Trotter, to build CD plant.

text.p: Zomax Optical Media Inc said Wednesday it acquired Trotter Technologies Inc for an undisclosed amount of cash and stock, and plans to build a compact disc facility in conjuction with the purchase.

Trotter, based in San Jose, California, is a return merchandise processing, warehousing and distribution (RMA services) company serving the software publishing market. It had 1996 revenues of $3.0 million. The acquisition was effective on May 1.

Zomax said it plans to build a compact disc replicating facility, with CD production beginning in the third quarter of this year. The company said it has space next to the Trotter facility in San Jose.

"The acquisition of Trotter with its RMA servicing and developing a CD facility in San Jose will position us to fully service our existing customer base on the West Coast," James Anderson, president and chief executive of Zomax, said in a statement. "We continue to seek the right opportunity in the East."
